sources.cite: Google Cloud documentation, Set up and manage VPC Network Peering
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: gcloud compute networks peerings update accepts --export-custom-routes and --import-custom-routes; '--import-custom-routes tells the network to accept custom routes from the peered network'; for exports 'The peered network must be set to import the routes' and for imports 'The peered network must export the routes first'. The VPC routes page (read 2026-11-18): peering dynamic routes are 'imported with custom route exchange from networks connected using VPC Network Peering'. That on-premises needs the peered range in Cloud Router's custom advertisements for the return path is the author's (the page does not say it; to verify against the Cloud Router advertisement page).

brief.situation: You are the network engineer at Fennick Outdoor. The new analytics-vpc is peered with hub-vpc, which reaches the data center over Dedicated Interconnect through Cloud Router cr-hub. Tonight's month-end Dataproc job in analytics-vpc must read the on-premises ledger database (10.12.8.20:1521) starting at 20:00. A test connection from analytics-vpc times out.
handover: Security policy: on-premises databases are never exposed to the internet.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows analytics-vpc, the peering with hub-vpc, the Interconnect and the routes in each direction.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: The month-end job starts at 20:00, 100 minutes after the failed test.

writeup.question: For the record: why analytics could not reach the ledger, what you changed in each direction, and why not a public path.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: analytics-vpc only had the hub's subnet routes: the peering exported and imported no custom routes, so the on-premises routes cr-hub learned stayed in the hub. And cr-hub advertised only 10.0.0.0/20, so the data center had no route back to 10.60.0.0/20.

parts.label: Changed
parts.modelAnswer: Export custom routes on hub-to-an, import on an-to-hub, and 10.60.0.0/20 added to cr-hub's advertisements. A Connectivity Test and a query passed.

parts.label: Not public
parts.modelAnswer: NAT to a public IP would have exposed the ledger to the internet; an egress firewall rule does nothing without a route.

expertPath.text: No 10.12.0.0/16 route in analytics; peering exchanges no custom routes; cr-hub advertises only the hub; test unreachable.
Export and import custom routes; advertise 10.60.0.0/20; Terraform and checklist.

ledgerExposed.headline: Route through the hub, not around it
ledgerExposed.body: The Interconnect was there; the routes were not shared. Exchange custom routes over the peering and advertise the range back, instead of exposing the database.

closeSlipped.headline: Peering does not share learned routes by default
closeSlipped.body: Routes Cloud Router learns in the hub cross a peering only if the hub exports and the spoke imports custom routes, and the data center needs the spoke's range advertised for the reply.

routed.headline: Good: both directions of routing
routed.body: You read the routes and the peering flags, enabled export and import, advertised the return range, confirmed with a Connectivity Test and a query, and put it in Terraform.

scoring.modelReasoning: analytics-vpc has no route to the data center because the peering exchanges only subnet routes: the hub must export custom routes (which include the routes Cloud Router learned) and analytics must import them. The data center also needs analytics' range advertised by Cloud Router for the reply. Configure both and test with a Connectivity Test. A public NAT path exposes the ledger; a firewall rule cannot fix a missing route.
